caregiverInfantBoundary: 0–2 support stays caregiver-facing in the strongest home language; no infant Thai target or screen activity
cultureApproach: Context and reciprocal respect, not a national-personality checklist
Do not grade children on cultural obedience
Cultural politeness never removes a person's right to seek help
No forced religious practice or public role-play disclosure
Thai language proficiency is separate from intelligence and age
assetPolicy: Link and map first. No imported provider PDFs/video/audio without asset-level permission.

questions: Which recent everyday conversation was hardest? No names or private documents needed.
Which home language and spoken/written format is easiest?
What do children and caregivers need to ask teachers?
Which situations differ between your school, workplace or neighbourhood?
Can this phone play short audio, and when is data available?
What important situation did our questions miss?
pilotResearch.limits: Purposive interviews inform design; they do not estimate population prevalence or establish learning effectiveness.

firstBuildRecommendation: After research and language review, prototype TH01 and TH02 as original private practice scenarios; keep wider YDC intact.
